goal: Adds a -v2onlyclearnet option so outbound connections to IPv4/IPv6 peers must use encrypted BIP324 (v2) transport.
Aimed at operators who want protection from passive traffic inspection (ISPs, firewalls, censors).
reviewability: Needs rebase, and the design itself (should this force -listen=0?) is still contested.
Maintainers explicitly postponed it from v32 to v33 pending agreement on that question.
agreement: Many concept ACKs over two years (sipa, mzumsande, dergoegge, laanwj, kristapsk, fjahr, sedited, ViniciusCestarii, danielabrozzoni) but the core design choice is disputed.
gmaxwell states strong disagreement with coupling the option to listen=0, calling it an anti-feature.
mzumsande and ViniciusCestarii favor an alternative (allow v2-only inbound) instead of the author's chosen approach.
Author has surveyed the tradeoffs but not yet converged with reviewers, and maintainers postponed merge pending consensus (mzumsande, sedited).

result.summary: Adds a -v2onlyclearnet startup option that prevents the node from making (or falling back to) v1/plaintext outbound connections to IPv4/IPv6 peers, while still allowing v1 on Tor/I2P/CJDNS since those are already encrypted. The option requires -listen=0 to avoid the risk of a v1-only eclipse attack surface, and includes an IsClearnet() helper, init-time validation, and functional tests. The PR has been open since September 2024 and has gone through several implementation approaches (outbound+inbound v2-only, then outbound-only) based on extensive review feedback.
result.problem: Users concerned about passive network observers (ISPs, firewalls, censors) inspecting or fingerprinting their Bitcoin traffic currently have no way to guarantee all outbound clearnet connections are encrypted; v1 fallback silently defeats BIP324's privacy goal. Roughly 70% of reachable nodes already support v2, making an opt-in enforcement option newly practical.

open_concerns: Whether the option should force -listen=0 (current approach, 'option A') or instead allow only v2 inbound while permitting listening ('option B'); gmaxwell, mzumsande, ViniciusCestarii, andrewtoth, davidgumberg have weighed in without consensus.
gmaxwell's structural objection that tying a privacy setting to giving up listening capacity is counterproductive for the network, not addressed by a code change.
Whether DNS-seed/fixed-seed addresses should be treated as v2 by default so v2-only nodes can bootstrap peers (raised by gmaxwell, partially addressed by merged PR #35766).
resolved_concerns: Earlier Concept NACK from vasild (fear that v2-only gives a false sense of anonymity) was withdrawn after discussion clarified the option only protects against passive observers, not active ones.

Several code review nits from luke-jr, fjahr, w0xlt, danielabrozzoni, ajtowns were addressed in later pushes (helper function IsClearnet, error message wording, edge cases for unresolved proxy destinations).
discussion.author_status: active but currently needs to rebase; last force-push 2026-08-13 was 'just a rebase', substantive design comments from 2026-09-10 (ViniciusCestarii) not yet answered

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: Core P2P connection-management change: adds logic in CConnman to skip v1 outbound connections and v1 reconnections for clearnet peers, plus a new IsClearnet() netbase helper. Carries the P2P label.
categories.rationale: P2 because it is a real, substantial privacy-hardening option for operators concerned about passive traffic inspection, echoed by many long-standing contributors (sipa: 'reasonable to offer an outbound-v2-only option' now that v2 adoption is ~70%). It is not P1 because it's opt-in and narrow in its actual privacy guarantee (does not hide that a node runs Bitcoin, per vasild/davidgumberg), and the design is still contested rather than settled, meaning the durable value is uncertain until the listen=0 question is resolved.

categories.name: docs
categories.evidence: Includes a release-notes file and help text, but these are secondary to the code change; the PR's subject is behavior, not documentation.
categories.rationale: Not a docs-primary PR; release notes and help text are incidental to the net.cpp/net.h behavior change.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: Touches netbase.h/netbase.cpp (IsClearnet helper) but these are network-classification helpers used by p2p logic, not general utils/logging/args infrastructure.
categories.rationale: The netbase changes are p2p-scoped helpers (clearnet vs privacy-network classification), not shared cross-area utility infrastructure as the utils category defines it.

uncertainties: Whether the project will ultimately land on option A (current, tied to listen=0) or option B (allow v2-only inbound), which affects how much of the current diff survives review.
Exact weight to give the postponement to v33 versus ongoing concept engagement when scoring priority; treated here as a sign of contested design rather than lowered importance per the rules.
result.card: This PR adds a -v2onlyclearnet option forcing outbound IPv4/IPv6 connections to use encrypted BIP324 v2 transport, aimed at protecting node operators from passive traffic inspection by ISPs or censors; it requires -listen=0 in its current form. Discussion spans two years and 22 distinct reviewers, with broad concept support (sipa, laanwj, kristapsk, dergoegge, fjahr, sedited) but a live, unresolved dispute over whether coupling the option to -listen=0 is sound design (gmaxwell strongly objects, mzumsande and ViniciusCestarii prefer an alternative allowing v2-only inbound). Maintainers explicitly postponed the PR from v32 to v33 because of this disagreement, and it currently needs a rebase. The strongest evidence of importance is the project's own stated goal for BIP324 adoption and the fact that ~70% of reachable nodes already support v2, making enforcement newly viable, but the PR's fate hinges on resolving the design dispute rather than further code review.
